title: Align homepage shell, navigation, and hero with Figma
context: The homepage root page at `/` should better match the existing Figma desktop and mobile frames. Figma sources: desktop https://www.figma.com/design/0J2JF0nYrI8EJrttdHNes4/Portfolio?node-id=1-549&t=AL7MiQ7CLvTxT4Cf-0 and mobile https://www.figma.com/design/0J2JF0nYrI8EJrttdHNes4/Portfolio?node-id=79-219&t=AL7MiQ7CLvTxT4Cf-0. Desktop should match closely, mobile should match the mobile frame, and tablet should scale from mobile using Figma auto-layout as a guide. This plan covers the foundational page background, fixed nav behavior, top gradient treatment, and hero sizing/positioning.

tasks.title: Apply the homepage background and hero cutaway treatment
acceptance_criteria: The main homepage background uses `--color-background` with `/images/nnnoise.svg` layered above it
The existing hero cutaway no longer reveals an incorrect texture or mismatched background
The hero uses a clip-path or equivalent CSS treatment to match the Figma cutaway shape based on the rotated rectangle
The background and cutaway treatment remain visually continuous across desktop, tablet, and mobile widths
`npm run verify` passes after the change

tasks.title: Update fixed navigation and top hero gradient behavior
acceptance_criteria: The site nav is fixed over the homepage hero
On desktop, nav spacing matches the current layout intent while the hero fits underneath without content collision
On mobile, the nav is transparent at the top of the page
The hero includes a black-to-transparent top gradient that is fully black behind the nav element
On mobile, the nav gains a black background that fades in on scroll
Keyboard focus states remain visible and accessible with the fixed nav treatment
`npm run verify` passes after the change

tasks.title: Match hero sizing, headline position, and scroll indicator spacing
acceptance_criteria: On desktop, the hero height is 95vh
On desktop, the hero headline is centered in the hero area relative to the Figma composition
On desktop, the scroll indicator sits near the bottom of the hero as shown in Figma
On mobile, hero spacing follows the Figma mobile frame rather than viewport-height sizing
On mobile, the headline does not use a max-width that causes unwanted wrapping compared with Figma
The headline gradient stops visually match Figma more closely, including the appearance of stops spanning the total headline width rather than only individual gradient words
`npm run verify` passes after the change
